body.rationale: Governing IPS (config/ips.yaml) is still a draft, so I weight compliance as provisional but still informative. First choice is resampled_efficient_frontier. It has no hard IPS breaches, tracking error of 4.33%, and effective N of 13.3, the broadest of any compliant return-based method. Its main weakness is that the CMA bias passes through resampling (inter-category review), and the gamma-tuning wording is muddled. Neither is disqualifying, and the CIO can rely on the covariance structure and the resampling to damp estimation error. That fits the late-cycle preference for covariance-based reasoning in §4.3. Second is black_litterman, which is compliant with 3.01% TE and a 0.70 backtest Sharpe. Its reviewed flaws, the gamma inconsistency and the volatility floor margin, are fixable. Third is cvar_minimization, which is compliant and has the best backtest Sharpe among the compliant methods (0.74) and a moderate -18.7% drawdown. It is also a non-traditional method, which helps the family-span rule. Its concentration (eff. N 2.9) and the thin tail sample are real concerns. Fourth is tail_risk_parity: it breaches the draft IPS on return, volatility and TE, but it is the best-behaved of the defensive forecast-free methods. It has 6.0 effective N, a -7.2% drawdown, and a low CRO risk of 0.29. It adds a downside-aware sleeve that the return-optimised candidates lack. Fifth is inverse_volatility. It is the broadest of the risk-based heuristics (eff. N 7.6, -9% drawdown) and a sensible hedge against model risk, although its IPS breaches and the cash-volatility sensitivity noted in its review keep it low. I put the first choice above the fifth because resampled_efficient_frontier is IPS-compliant and has a 13.3 effective N with a 4.33% TE. Inverse_volatility fails three hard constraints and has TE of 6.90%, so the CIO would have to repair it before use. I left out max_sharpe because of its 46% single-style bet and the Sharpe labelling problem, and I left out market_cap_weight because of the -40.6% drawdown and the 0.80 CRO risk. I flag hierarchical_risk_parity. It holds 91.9% cash with 1.4 effective assets, a 0.65% volatility and a 0.14 Sharpe. It breaches three hard constraints, and its own proposal concedes that the cash weight is the method working mechanically, not diversification. The CIO should not lean on it.
